title: possible water/germ/food entry at point of handle & plastic overlay
text:
possible water/germ/food entry at point of handle & plastic overlay. KitchenAid makes a good ice cream scoop. I have this in the color, Pistachio.

It is a metal scoop with a plastic overlay on the handle. I was perplexed by those mentioning

1. water possibly getting into handle
2. plastic pulls away from handle.

I went in for a closer look and sure enough, these things happen. I placed the scoop in a mason jar filled with water, waiting 20 minutes and checked. I would not have noticed this before since I never let my scoops sit in water, and I don't put them through the dishwasher (in the past, doing so seemed to make them get pit marks, especially if it was an aluminum variety). So I hand wash...It's ice cream.. I just rinse and dry and then back in the drawer it goes. I may use it 10 times a year, and that's if I don't use a spoon to dig out ice cream. Anyway, I took scoop out from water, dried it, and shook it. I thought I could hear something. So then proceeded to pull on the handle to try to separate metal from plastic, and sure enough a couple drops of water came out.

As for plastic overlay pulling away from the metal, that does happen but only if you are looking to do so. I took it a step further and twisted and pulled to see how far I could go with it. No damage. I doubt it will ever fall part. However, the fact that it can be manipulated means that it is a pressure seal. It is likely why it is "possible" for water to get in. It isn't going to happen by just rinsing it. I bet I never ever experience that outside of this contrived experiment due to the way I handle my scoop. BUT if you are inclined to run it through the dishwasher or let it sit in the sink with water, then your experience may vary. No one should need to even be concerned with that, so I can't rate fully based on that.

It does get really good rating across several "best of" articles. OXO seems to win out, but this is considered a good one. I think it is a good one. I like the feel of the handle. It feels just a tiny bit heavier than my older Farberware one. It definitely cuts through hard ice cream. The slightly wider, thicker grips gives me a better grip. I do wonder if the handle may be too smooth for some people.

As a rarely used item, I will have this a long time. As a rarely used item I am more liberal with what is acceptable, particularly since it is just a means to grab some ice cream. However, I'm a little grossed out at the possibility of water or other gunk possibly building up where the handle and plastic overlay meet. It takes two hands to demonstrate it, so I would need assistance to take a picture. I don't know if it is a design flaw, over sight, or somehow intentional (the extra gives allows more pressure to be place into handle to scoop extra hard ice cream)?

I do love KitchenAid, and I normally highly recommend their wares. But this item of this design style does not impress me like everything else.

Again- great feel, good grip, cuts into hard ice cream, typical scoop shape, attractive

BUT, that spot where steel meets plastic.. Nope.

3 stars.
